title: Cash Credit vs Overdraft: Key Differences Every Business Owner Should Know
excerpt: Cash credit and overdraft both provide flexible borrowing, but they differ in security, purpose, and pricing. Understand which facility suits your business model.

blocks.text: Indian businesses commonly use cash credit (CC) and overdraft (OD) for short-term funding, yet many owners treat them as interchangeable. They are not — each product has distinct security requirements, interest calculation methods, and renewal processes. Choosing the wrong facility increases cost and compliance burden.
Cash Credit Explained

Cash credit is a working capital limit secured primarily against stock (inventory) and book debts (receivables). The limit is calculated using turnover methods and reviewed quarterly or annually. Interest applies only on the daily utilised balance. You submit stock statements and debtor ageing reports as ongoing compliance.
Overdraft Explained

Overdraft is a facility on your current account allowing withdrawals beyond available balance up to a sanctioned limit. Security is often property, fixed deposits, or securities — not stock. OD suits businesses needing flexible buffer cash without detailed stock reporting, or professionals with salaried income plus business income.
Quick Comparison

items: CC: Secured against stock/debtors; OD: Often secured against property or FD
CC: Requires periodic stock statements; OD: Minimal ongoing reporting
CC: Designed for trading and manufacturing WC; OD: General-purpose flexibility
CC: Drawing power linked to stock value; OD: Fixed limit regardless of inventory
Both: Interest on utilised amount only; both: Renewable annually

blocks.text: Consultants assess your business type — trading firms often need CC; service businesses with property may prefer OD. Some borrowers benefit from holding both facilities for different purposes.

title: How Cash Credit Facilities Help Manage Seasonal Business Fluctuations
excerpt: Seasonal businesses face cash crunches during peak stocking periods. Cash credit provides revolving limits that expand and contract with your inventory cycle.

blocks.text: Agriculture traders, festival goods suppliers, winter apparel dealers, and tax-season service firms experience predictable revenue spikes and troughs. During peak season, you must stock heavily before sales arrive — creating a temporary cash gap. Term loans are poorly suited to this cycle because you pay interest on full amount even when needs drop. Cash credit matches seasonal rhythm.
How CC Supports Seasonal Cycles

items: Draw funds to purchase peak-season inventory; repay as sales convert to cash
Pay interest only on daily outstanding — not on the full sanctioned limit
Renew limit before season based on projected higher turnover
Maintain supplier relationships with timely payments during stocking phase
Avoid selling at distress discounts due to cash shortage

blocks.text: Planning for Seasonal Limits

Apply for limit enhancement 2–3 months before peak season with projected sales data and prior season performance. Banks need evidence that post-season collections will clear the outstanding. Historical bank credits during previous seasons strengthen your case.
Consultants help present seasonal business cases to credit committees — translating your sales calendar into limit requirements banks understand and approve.

title: Documents Required for Cash Credit Account Opening
excerpt: Opening a cash credit account requires KYC, financial statements, and security documentation. Prepare this checklist before visiting the bank.

blocks.text: Cash credit account opening is more document-intensive than opening a simple current account because the bank extends a revolving credit limit secured against business assets. Incomplete files are the primary cause of delayed sanction. Prepare documents in advance and ensure consistency across all submissions.
KYC and Business Proof

items: PAN card and Aadhaar of all partners/directors and authorised signatories
Partnership deed / MOA-AOA / LLP agreement and certificate of incorporation
GST registration certificate and Udyam registration
Shop establishment licence or trade licence where applicable
Address proof for business premises and residence of promoters

blocks.text: Financial Documents

items: ITR with computation for last 2–3 years
Audited financial statements — balance sheet and P&L
GST returns GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B for last 12 months
Bank statements of all business accounts for 12 months
Existing loan statements and sanction letters if any
Projected turnover and stock statement format for limit calculation

blocks.text: Security Documentation

Hypothecation agreement on stock and book debts, collateral security if required (property papers, FD lien), and insurance on stock where mandated. Consultants verify document completeness against specific bank checklists before submission — reducing rejection and re-work cycles.

title: Tips to Increase Your Cash Credit Limit with Banks
excerpt: Need a higher cash credit limit? Banks review turnover growth, repayment discipline, and stock management. Use these strategies to justify limit enhancement.

blocks.text: As your business grows, your original cash credit limit may constrain operations — forcing you to delay purchases or use expensive informal credit. Banks enhance limits when you demonstrate increased turnover, clean account conduct, and proper stock statement compliance. Proactive preparation beats last-minute emergency requests.
Strategies for Limit Enhancement

items: Maintain zero overdue days and avoid cheque returns on your CC account
Submit stock and debtor statements on time every month or quarter
Route increased sales through the account — visible turnover growth supports higher limits
Present audited financials showing improved margins and net worth
Offer additional collateral if the bank requires comfort for higher exposure
Apply 60–90 days before you need the enhanced limit — not during a crisis

blocks.text: When to Consider a Second Lender

If your primary bank caps exposure or demands unreasonable collateral, a parallel CC facility with another lender may diversify capacity. Total banking exposure across lenders must remain serviceable from cash flow. Consultants model combined interest cost and compliance workload before recommending dual facilities.
Regular annual review meetings with your RM — facilitated by a consultant who speaks credit language — keep your limit aligned with business scale.

title: Understanding Cash Credit Interest Calculation Methods
excerpt: Cash credit interest is charged on daily utilised balance, but rate structures vary. Learn how banks calculate CC interest and what affects your effective cost.

blocks.text: Unlike term loans with fixed EMIs, cash credit interest fluctuates monthly based on how many days you utilised the limit and at what average balance. Understanding this calculation helps you minimise interest by timing repayments and managing drawing power efficiently.
Daily Product Method

Most banks apply: Interest = (Daily utilised balance × Annual rate × Days) / 365. Each day's closing debit balance in the CC account contributes to the sum. Credit entries reduce utilisation immediately — so collecting receivables into the CC account saves interest from that day onward.
Components Affecting Your Rate

items: Base rate or MCLR/EBLR linked rate plus spread assigned to your account
Annual review charges and processing fees on limit renewal
Penal interest if utilisation exceeds drawing power due to stock statement shortfall
Commitment charges on unutilised limit — some banks charge if usage falls below minimum threshold
GST on interest and service charges as applicable

blocks.text: Interest Saving Practices

Park collections in the CC account before transferring to savings. Time major vendor payments after receivable inflows. Avoid maintaining high utilisation during low-activity periods — consider temporary repayment from surplus funds. Consultants review your CC account statements to identify interest leakage and suggest operational tweaks.

title: Why Small Businesses Prefer Cash Credit Over Term Loans
excerpt: For ongoing working capital needs, cash credit often beats term loans in flexibility and cost. Discover why SMEs across India rely on CC facilities.

blocks.text: Small businesses face continuous working capital needs — not one-time lump sums. Term loans disburse fully on day one and charge interest on the entire amount throughout tenure, even when you no longer need the funds. Cash credit aligns with how trading and manufacturing SMEs actually use money: draw when needed, repay when cash arrives, repeat.
Flexibility Advantages

items: Revolving nature — repay and re-borrow within limit without new applications
Interest only on amount used, not full sanctioned limit
Limit scales with business growth through periodic reviews
No fixed EMI pressure during slow months when utilisation naturally drops
Integrated with current account — seamless vendor payments and collections

blocks.text: When Term Loans Still Make Sense

Use term loans for specific capital expenditure — machinery, vehicles, renovation — where you need a fixed amount for a defined purpose. Use cash credit for inventory, receivables gap, and operational float. Mixing them incorrectly — funding stock with a term loan — increases total interest cost.

Loan consultants design optimal debt structure: CC for working capital core, term loans for asset purchases, and OD as emergency buffer — creating a balanced, cost-efficient credit portfolio for your SME.
